correctness.rationale: For a four-consecutive-input binary rule, the length-three input suffix is the complete state for extending a free input block. Start from all eight suffixes; following an output word by taking every matching appended-bit edge gives exactly its possible terminal suffixes. The empty subset is therefore equivalent to absence, and breadth-first search gives the least length. If no empty subset is reachable, every finite word occurs. For any specified bilateral output, the closed nonempty constraints for growing windows then have a common preimage by compactness. An independently written exhaustive implementation (replay: python3 /workspace/branches/6ff72d77-5aa8-42e3-832c-8993681940cb/independent_census.py; full-run.log in the same directory) reproduced all histogram bins from all 65,536 tables, including 0 at 15 and 582 at infinity. The maximal finite length was 18, attained by 5482, 22184, 43351 and 60053. Each has zero missing words at length 17 and eight at 18; both stated witnesses were independently checked for both rules to which each was assigned. Fullness at length 17 implies fullness at shorter lengths. The uploaded scripts were inspected, not executed; the independent check requires neither periodic boundaries nor extrapolation from a rule sample.

value.rationale: A uniform minimal-obstruction cutoff gives the exact block length sufficient to test surjectivity for every four-input binary rule and shows why a length-17 test is insufficient. Four inputs are the next full binary family beyond three-input elementary rules; the census supplies a reproducible baseline with sharp witnesses and a missing interior length, not merely a rerun of the known Boolean surjectivity census.
